verdict: NEEDS_REREAD: coverage is real and mostly accurate (all 30 files in DroppyCode/Services/Providers are assigned, line counts match `wc -l` exactly), but R041 misstates the Claude handshake argv, R044 omits two whole algorithms (the Copilot model filter and the entire account.getQuota percent/skip logic), and several load-bearing details (persisted-seed identity, dead per-turn state, fallback auth branches) are missing across R039/R043/R046.
gaps: R041 / ClaudeSession.swift:185-193 - the handshake argv is described as "the argv omits --include-partial-messages and adds --no-session-persistence". It is not a delta of the session argv: it is a fixed, much shorter list `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --setting-sources user,project,local`, with no --permission-prompt-tool, no --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, no --permission-mode, no --mcp-config, no --append-system-prompt. A port following the report's wording would launch the catalog probe with the full session argv.

R041 / ClaudeSession.swift:201-204 - handshake() requires `response.commands` to be a non-nil array before it will return anything; if the CLI answers the initialize without a `commands` array it throws "Claude could not load its commands." even though the caller (ProviderRegistry.loadClaudeCatalog, ProviderRegistry.swift:498-502) only wants `.models`. The report records the two error strings but never states that a missing `commands` key kills the Claude model catalog too.

R044 / CopilotSession.swift:407 - listModels skips every entry where `model["policy"]["state"] == "disabled"`. The report lists `.policy.state` among the fields read and documents the "unconfigured" detail string, but never mentions the disabled filter, so a port would surface models the CLI will refuse.

R044 / CopilotSession.swift:444-467 - readPlanLimits has no entry at all in feature_notes. Missing: a snapshot is skipped when `isUnlimitedEntitlement == true` or when `entitlementRequests` is absent or <= 0; percent is `max(0, min(100, 100 - remainingPercentage))` when remainingPercentage exists, otherwise `min(100, usedRequests / entitlementRequests * 100)`; `resetDate` is parsed with a plain ISO8601DateFormatter and then retried with `formatOptions = [.withFullDate]` (CopilotSession.swift:470-475); the whole read returns nil when no window survives; and the plan name is a SECOND request (account.getCurrentAuth) whose `authInfo.copilotUser.copilot_plan` is wrapped as "Copilot <plan>".

R044 / CopilotSession.swift:428-439 - authStatus's non-happy paths are undocumented: a failed connect() returns .unknown, a failed account.getCurrentAuth request returns .unknown, and a null or missing `authInfo` returns .signedOut. Only the " · no Copilot access" suffix made it into the report.

R046 / ProviderRegistry.swift:780 - the opencode auth branch's fallback is stated only as far as the credential parse. When no U+25CF line is found the result is `result.succeeded ? .signedOut : .unknown`, not an unconditional .signedOut. A port that hardcodes .signedOut will show "Not signed in" for a CLI that merely failed to run.

R043 / CommandCodeAPI.swift:349-359 - the report gives the nine seed detail strings but never the seed ids or names. Those exact ids are load-bearing twice over: they are what goes into the persisted "providerModelCatalogs" blob, and ProviderRegistry.loadCatalog compares `models(for: .commandcode) == Self.commandcodeSeed` (ProviderRegistry.swift:464) to decide whether to re-probe. The ids are claude-sonnet-5 (isDefault), claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, google/gemini-3.8-flash, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, moonshotai/kimi-k3, zai-org/glm-5.3, with names "Claude Sonnet 5", "Claude Fable 5.1", "Claude Opus 5", "GPT-6 Astra", "GPT-5.6 Sol", "Gemini 3.8 Flash", "DeepSeek V4 Flash", "Kimi K3", "GLM 5.3".

R039 / AntigravitySession.swift:23-24, 88, 150-151 - the report says runtimeMode and interactionMode are "refreshed on each send". They are written on every send and then never read: modeArguments is called once at line 88 with `configuration.runtimeMode` / `configuration.interactionMode`, so the two stored properties are dead after init. The practical consequence for the port (a mid-thread runtime-mode or plan/build switch cannot reach `agy` without relaunching the process) is not stated anywhere. Contrast PiSession.swift:279-288, where the same switch does take effect because it is rewritten into the gate file every turn.

R039 / ACPSession.swift:381-385 - applyConfigOptions sets `effortConfigID = nil` and `fastConfigID = nil` at the top of every call. A config_option_update or a set_config_option reply that omits the thought_level or model_config entries therefore drops the effort slider and the Fast toggle for the rest of the session. The report describes what the branches build but not this reset.

R039 / ACPSession.swift:534-535 - the `config_option_update` session/update notification is handled (it re-runs applyConfigOptions, which re-emits .models with a new current model / effort scale / fast tier). It appears only as the bare word "configOptions" inside persisted_fields; there is no feature note saying the agent can push a live model or effort change mid-session. `agent_thought_chunk`, `plan` and `available_commands_update` are likewise handled but never named in feature_notes.

R040 / OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:437-446, 471-482, 808-812 - no feature note covers cancellation. interrupt() sets `interrupted`, cancels sendTask, roundTask and sseDrain, and resumes every pending approval continuation with `false` (i.e. an in-flight approval is silently treated as a decline); stop() does all that plus sets isStopping and nils sessionID, which makes isRunning false (line 240). finishInterrupted resolves approvals the same way and emits .turnCompleted(.interrupted). Also unstated: `approveAllRemaining` (set by the "always" option at line 450) is reset per turn at line 292, which is what makes the label "Approve for turn" honest.

R046 / ProviderRegistry.swift:626-641 - refreshCredits has no 25-second watchdog and no `defer` around `loadingCredits.remove(provider)` (unlike refreshPlanLimits at lines 550-566), and when the key is empty it clears `credits[provider]` but leaves `creditsFetchedAt[provider]` intact. The report flattens both reads into "the read runs on its own task" and states only the credits-clearing half.
contradictions: R042 (CodexSession) and R044 (CopilotSession) both file `sendsVersion:` as an unresolved question ("whether sendsVersion: false omits the jsonrpc version field or some client-version field"). It is settled one grep away in an adjacent bundle: JSONRPC.swift:109 `if sendsVersion { message["jsonrpc"] = "2.0" }`. Codex's app-server is the only connection built with `sendsVersion: false` (CodexSession.swift:508) and therefore must receive frames with NO `jsonrpc` member, while ACP (ACPSession.swift:117) and Copilot (CopilotSession.swift:494) must receive `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`. Two reports leaving this open risks the port sending a uniform envelope.

R041 asks who populates PlanLimits.Window.detail ("declared with default nil but never set anywhere in this file"); R040 answers it for Z.ai (ZaiAPI window details "<current> of <usage> credits" / "<current> of <usage> calls"). Not a factual conflict, but the two reports were not reconciled, so the family leaves a field looking unused when it is not.

R041 asks which readers call PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes:); R040 (ZaiAPI) and R045 (PiPlanLimits, "Codex · " + windowTitle(minutes: limit_window_seconds / 60)) and R042 (Codex plan windows) all name callers. Same unreconciled-question pattern.

R044's header note claims "session delete was verified live" and then admits no session.delete call exists in the file; nothing else in the family accounts for a Copilot session ever being deleted. Either the header comment is stale or the delete lives outside Services/Providers and no reader in this family chased it.
cross_cutting_findings: Three different JSON-RPC dialects ride on the same JSONRPCConnection with different envelopes and framings, and the port must keep them apart: ACP (ACPSession.swift:117, sendsVersion true, default framing), Codex app-server (CodexSession.swift:508, sendsVersion FALSE, default framing), Copilot SDK (CopilotSession.swift:494, sendsVersion true, StdioProcess framing: .contentLength). Pi and Command Code and Antigravity use line/JSONL framing instead (PiSession.swift framing: .lines).

Every unsupported inbound JSON-RPC request is answered with error code -32601, but the message differs by provider: ACPSession.swift:559 sends "Method not found"; CodexSession and CopilotSession send "Droppy Code does not support <method>." A port should not unify these.

The client identity string "droppy-code" / title "Droppy Code" / version AppInfo.version is sent on four separate handshakes with different key paths: ACP `clientInfo` in initialize, Codex `clientInfo` in initialize (CodexSession.swift:517), Copilot `clientName` in session.create/resume plus the ping payload `{"message":"droppy-code"}` (CopilotSession.swift:496), Claude control request ids prefixed "droppy-code-<n>".

RuntimeMode.rawValue and InteractionMode.rawValue are an on-disk contract, not just an in-memory enum: PiSession.swift:281-286 writes them verbatim into the per-session gate JSON, and the shipped TypeScript in PiCLI.extensionSource compares them against the literals "fullAccess", "autoAcceptEdits", "auto" and "plan". No report in this family states that those raw values must match exactly, and the enum is declared outside the bundle.

Four independent "install a helper file next to the app, only when the bytes differ" patterns exist and must all be ported: CommandCodeAPI.installMod() writing droppy-code-approvals.ts, PiCLI.installExtension() writing droppy-gate.ts, MCPBridge.installBridge(), plus the per-session scratch directories (Command Code approvals dir, Pi gates dir). All are under Application Support on macOS.

Runtime-mode changes reach the provider by three different mechanisms, and only one survives without restarting the process: a live protocol call (Claude set_permission_mode, Copilot session.permissions.setMode, Codex per-turn approvalPolicy/sandboxPolicy, ACP set_config_option), a rewritten gate file (Pi, Command Code), or launch flags only (Antigravity, ACP launchArguments, Copilot isExperimentalMode). Antigravity and the ACP launch flags need a session restart; the family never says so in one place.

Only two providers expose a cancellable, interruptible turn over the wire (Claude control `interrupt`, Codex `turn/interrupt`, Copilot `session.abort`, ACP `session/cancel`, Pi `abort`). Antigravity and Command Code have no interrupt message at all and rely on SIGTERM plus an isStopping/interruptRequested flag to keep the UI from reporting a crash (AntigravitySession.swift:165-175, CommandCodeSession.swift:229-236). A Windows port has no SIGTERM equivalent with those semantics and must decide what replaces it.

Three providers pass MCP configuration by three different channels that all originate in the same settings: --mcp-config + --strict-mcp-config (Claude), config.mcp_servers inside thread params (Codex), --allowed-mcp-server-names <ids...> (Antigravity), MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments() (Copilot), MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment() merged into the child env (opencode), GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH (antigravity), and DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE / DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG env vars read by the Pi and Command Code helper scripts.

Two UserDefaults keys and one alternate defaults suite carry the whole provider cache: "providerModelCatalogs" and "providerModelCatalogDates" on UserDefaults.standard, "recentSlashCommands" on (CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard) (ProviderRegistry.swift:47-49, 158, 697). The catalogs blob is rewritten whole on every change, and at load time every cached row is re-sorted through ACPSession.orderedEfforts (ProviderRegistry.swift:167-172) - a migration step that only exists as that one map call.
thin_reports: R044 (CopilotSession.swift, 1075 lines) - dense and accurate on the event stream and permission model, but the static half of the file is compressed almost to nothing: listModels, authStatus and readPlanLimits (CopilotSession.swift:400-475) get field lists in persisted_fields and title strings in ui_elements, with no feature note describing their actual logic. The disabled-model filter and the entire quota percent/skip computation are absent. Needs a targeted re-read of lines 400-475.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD - the three reports are mostly accurate and unusually specific, but R037 states a provider-config rule that the source contradicts, R038 states the wrong field-value fallback chain for MCPStore, and the OAuth callback page's verbatim assets plus several protocol field names, unreachable branches and dead APIs are missing.
contradictions: R037 vs source, MCPProviderConfig.swift:129-133: R037's feature_notes say "Claude, Codex and Gemini omit an empty env or headers object entirely". False for Gemini remote servers - `gemini(_:)` emits `"headers": .object(server.headers.mapValues(JSONValue.string))` unconditionally, exactly like Copilot (:60). Only the Gemini LOCAL branch guards `env` with `if !server.env.isEmpty` (:139). R037 also contradicts itself: its persisted_fields line for Gemini says `remote {httpUrl, headers}` with no optionality marker while the feature note says it is omitted. A port following the feature note writes a different gemini-settings.json than Droppy does.

R038 vs source, MCPStore.swift:64-70: R038 describes `value(for:of:)` as "draft first, else the Keychain secret for a .secret field, else the connection's stored value, else field.defaultValue". The source is an if/else-if: a `.secret` field reads ONLY the Keychain and never falls through to `connections[id]?.values[key]`; a non-secret field never reads the Keychain. Both kinds then fall to `field.defaultValue ?? ""`. The reported chain would make a port show a stale plaintext value for a secret field whose Keychain item is missing (including every CaptureRun, where MCPKeychain.value returns nil by design, MCPKeychain.swift:12).

R037 internal: its MCPProbe entry leaves "whether the 240-second mcp-remote deadline is ever reached in practice" unresolved, while its own MCPProviderConfig entry records that `mcp-remote` is minted only by `acpServers(allowsHTTP: false)` (MCPProviderConfig.swift:99). Those two facts together settle it - see the unreachable-branch gap below - but the report files them as an open question instead.
cross_cutting_findings: Path literals the three reports all deferred are resolvable and matter: `AppInfo.name` is `Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleDisplayName") as? String ?? "Droppy Code"` (Core/Support/Text.swift:4) and `Storage.root` is `~/Library/Application Support/<AppInfo.name>`, overridable by `CaptureRun.storageRoot` (Services/Store/Storage.swift:19-25). So mcp.json and custom-mcp.json sit directly in that folder and MCPPaths.directory is `<that>/mcp`.

Directory-case collision nobody flagged: `MCPBridge.installBridge()` writes to `<Application Support>/<AppInfo.name>/MCP/droppy-mcp-bridge.mjs` (MCPBridgeSource.swift:243-246, capital MCP, built from `FileManager.urls(for:.applicationSupportDirectory)` and NOT from Storage.root), while `MCPPaths.directory` is `Storage.root/mcp` (MCP.swift:231, lowercase). On a default case-insensitive macOS volume and on Windows these are the same folder, so the bridge .mjs lands beside claude.json / codex.json / copilot.json / gemini-settings.json / proxy-port / managed.json; on a case-sensitive volume they are two folders. A second consequence: under CaptureRun, MCPPaths moves with Storage.root but the bridge directory does not.

Complete file inventory under MCPPaths.directory, which no single report gives: claude.json, codex.json, copilot.json (MCP.swift:236-241), gemini-settings.json (MCPProviderConfig.swift:238), proxy-port (MCPProxy.swift:15), managed.json (MCPExternalSync.swift:52). `writeAll([])` deletes only the first four (MCPProviderConfig.swift:150-152); proxy-port is never deleted by anything, so a reinstall reuses the old port, and managed.json is deleted exactly once by the migration (MCPExternalSync.swift:27).

The consumer side of every generated artifact is unrecorded, so the port has the file formats but not the invocations: ClaudeSession.swift:96 passes `--mcp-config <path> --strict-mcp-config` (both flags, only when claudeConfigPath() is non-nil); AntigravitySession.swift:83-84 passes `--allowed-mcp-server-names` followed by connectedIDs(); ProviderRegistry.swift:274 sets `GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH` to gemini-settings.json (the Gemini file is consumed by the Antigravity provider, not a "Gemini" provider); ProviderRegistry.swift:272 merges opencodeEnvironment() for `.opencode`; CopilotSession.swift:486 appends copilotArguments(); CodexSession.swift:257-261 merges codexOverrides() into `params["config"]["mcp_servers"]`; ACPSession.swift:254 passes acpServers(allowsHTTP: supportsHTTPMCP) as the `mcpServers` field of session/new and session/load.

The env var that carries the bridge path is never named in any report: PiSession.swift:105-110 and CommandCodeSession.swift:174-179 set `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE` to the installed .mjs path, and set `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG` to MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path only when that file exists. R037 names DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG but not DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE.

MCPHub's only consumer is OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:510 (tools()), :898 (parse) and :904 (call) - the in-app model-API provider. R037 left that unresolved. MCPHub.terminateAll() is called from AppDelegate.swift:54.

Token expiry spans R037 and R038 and is mis-stated as unconditional: `storeSession` writes `expires_at` only when the token response carried `expires_in` (MCPOAuth.swift:698-700), and `accessToken` treats a missing `expires_at` as never-expiring (`guard let expiresAt = ... else { return false }`, MCPOAuth.swift:172). Combined with MCPProxy.swift:355-361, the proxy's "401 -> fetch token again and replay once" does NOT force a refresh; it calls the same `accessToken` and, absent an expiry, gets the identical cached token, so the replay is a byte-identical retry. Neither report states this.

Custom-server migration risk spans R032 and R038: `MCPCustomServer.Variable` uses the synthesized decoder with no default for `isSecret` (MCPCustom.swift:15-19), so a stored variable object missing that key throws; because the throw happens inside `decodeIfPresent([Variable]...)` (MCPCustom.swift:46,48) and `MCPStore.load()` decodes the whole array with `try?` (MCPStore.swift:245-248), one bad variable silently drops EVERY custom server, not one. R032 raised the decoder question; nobody carried it to the blast radius.
gaps: MCPCatalog.swift - no report records each field's `kind`, which decides whether a value goes to mcp.json or the Keychain. Exactly three built-in fields are non-secret: gitlab `instance` (.text, :31), filesystem `root` (.path, :83), sqlite `path` (.path, :389). Every other declared field is `.secret`, including postgres `url` (:372) and mongodb `url` (:407) whose values are full connection strings. So those three keys are the only ones that ever appear in `MCPConnection.values` in mcp.json for a built-in server. R032's persisted_fields lumps all field keys as "mcp.json values or Keychain entries".

MCPOAuth.swift:903 - the callback page's inline logo is a single `<path d="...">` of roughly 1.4 KB of exact coordinates. R037 paraphrases it ("a sprout/leaf mark plus two round dots (circle near 63,43 radius 5 ...)"). A parity port cannot reconstruct the mark from that; the `d` string must be captured verbatim, along with `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html lang="en">`, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`, `* { box-sizing: border-box; }` and `html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; }`, none of which R037 lists.

MCPOAuth.swift:19-44 - the error-message composition rule is missing. R037 prints a flat list of strings, but `discoveryFailed`, `metadataFailed`, `registrationFailed` and `tokenFailed` render as `<base> <detail>` when the detail is non-empty and `<base>` alone when empty, while `callbackFailed` and `network` render the DETAIL ALONE when non-empty and their base only when empty. So the user-visible text for a 404 during metadata lookup is "The server's sign-in details didn't make sense. The server answered 404.", not either string on its own.

MCPOAuth.swift:209-211, 225-232 - protected-resource metadata field names are only half recorded. R037 names `authorization_servers` and `resource` but not `scopes_supported` (the array whose non-empty strings become resourceScopes, which then drive both the registration `scope` and the authorization-URL `scope`), and it does not state that only the FIRST element of `authorization_servers` is used.

MCPProbe.swift:196-197 and :277-278 - the probe reads the server name and version from `result.serverInfo.name` and `result.serverInfo.version`. R037 says the probe "returns the server name, version" without ever naming the `serverInfo` object, so a port has no field path for the value it persists as `MCPConnection.serverVersion`.

MCPHub.swift:281 and MCPProbe.swift:89 - `checkReply` falls back to the literal string "unknown error" when a JSON-RPC error object has no `message`. That string reaches the user through LocalizedError (MCPHubError.server / MCPProbeError.malformed, which renders "The server sent something unexpected: unknown error"). Neither report lists it among the UI strings.

MCPProbe.swift:308 - `postJSON` builds `URLRequest(url:timeoutInterval: 30)` for every remote probe request. R037's MCPProbe timeout notes cover only the 240/90 second stdio deadlines and the 5 ms poll; the 30-second per-request HTTP timeout is absent, and it differs from MCPHub, which passes the per-call timeout (60/120/30) into its URLRequest (MCPHub.swift:453).

MCPProxy.swift:17-24 + MCP.swift:165 - the proxy-port file is written as a side effect of the FIRST read of `MCPProxy.port`, and that first read happens inside `MCPCatalogEntry.resolve` via `MCPProxy.url(for: id)`, i.e. potentially before `start()` is ever called. R038 records the file's format but presents it as proxy-lifecycle state rather than as something a pure-looking `resolve()` triggers.

MCPProxy.swift:118-128 + MCPStore.swift:22-27 - the repick path leaves the provider configs stale. `MCPStore.init` calls `MCPProxy.shared.start()` and then `exportAll()`, which bakes `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp/<id>` into claude.json, codex.json, copilot.json and gemini-settings.json. If the listener afterwards enters `.failed`, `repickPort()` moves the port and rewrites proxy-port, but nothing re-runs `MCPProviderConfig.writeAll`, so every config written this launch points at the dead port. Neither R038's proxy entry nor its store entry connects these.

MCPBridgeSource.swift:49-56, :74-151, :225-237 - the bridge never kills a spawned child. `withTimeout` rejects after CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 and `loadMCPTools` catches and skips the server, but there is no `child.kill()`, `unref()` or SIGTERM anywhere in the file (grep confirms zero hits), so a server that hangs during initialize or tools/list leaves a live process for the lifetime of the Pi / Command Code host. This is the opposite of MCPHub, which tracks every child in `liveProcesses` and SIGKILLs it at quit. R037 describes the timeout as a plain skip.

MCPBridgeSource.swift:154 - the bridge's `postMessage` sets only Content-Type and Accept (plus lowercase `mcp-session-id`). It does NOT send `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18`, which both MCPHub (:462) and MCPProbe (:314) do send. R037 lists the bridge's headers correctly but does not flag the divergence, which a port would silently normalize away.

MCPProxy.swift:308 and :369-378 - the proxy forwards the client's HTTP method verbatim, so GET (the streamable-HTTP SSE channel) and DELETE (session teardown) pass through unchanged; no report states which methods are supported. It also copies back only Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id and Cache-Control, so `WWW-Authenticate` on a 401 is dropped - any client that tried OAuth discovery through a proxy route would see a bare 401.

MCPProxy.swift:263-275 - `readBody` on an early EOF (`isComplete || error != nil`) forwards whatever bytes arrived, so a request truncated below its declared Content-Length is relayed upstream rather than refused. R038 documents the 413/411/400 refusals but not this silent-truncation path.

MCPHub.swift:59 vs :76-95 - the `failed` set is consulted only by `tools()`; `call()` never checks it, so a server whose `listTools` threw is still launched again on a direct tool call. Separately, the `didRestart`/`dead` one-restart policy lives entirely in `ensureStdio` (:307-319): the HTTP path (:419-450) has no restart or dead state at all, and `initialized` is only cleared by `stop()`. R037 presents the restart policy without scoping it to stdio.

MCPStore.swift:335 - on probe success, `connectedAt`, `serverVersion` and `tools` are written only `if var connection = connections[entry.id]` exists, while `states[entry.id] = .connected(toolCount:)` is set unconditionally. A probe that succeeds with no connection row therefore shows as connected but is filtered out of `enabledServers` (which requires `connectedAt != nil`, :42) and so reaches no provider config. R038 states the success path without the guard.

MCPKeychain.swift:37-49 - `set()` calls `SecItemUpdate` with a query that carries no `kSecAttrAccessible`; only the `SecItemAdd` fallback (:47) applies `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked`. An item created by an earlier build keeps whatever accessibility it had forever. R037 records the add attribute but not that updates never migrate it - a persisted attribute whose migration behavior is unstated.

Unreachable / dead code nobody classified, which the contract explicitly asks for: (a) `MCPProxy.stop()` (MCPProxy.swift:142) has no call site anywhere in the repository - the proxy is never shut down; R038 raised it as a question rather than resolving it. (b) `MCPOAuth.refreshIfNeeded(serverID:)` (MCPOAuth.swift:193) has no call site anywhere; R037 documents it as shipped behavior. (c) `MCPProxy.Route.headers` is always `[:]` at both registration sites (MCPStore.swift:284 and :310), so route-configured headers are dead configuration. (d) MCPProbe's `isOAuth` branch - the 240-second deadline (MCPProbe.swift:115) and the stderr "Unauthorized"/"invalid_grant" -> unauthorizedOAuth mapping (:217-219) - is unreachable for every built-in server: the only producer of a `mcp-remote` argument is `MCPProviderConfig.acpServers(allowsHTTP: false)` (:99), whose output goes to ACPSession.swift:254 and never to the probe, and the probe's sole caller (MCPStore.swift:313) always passes `entry.resolve(values:)`. Only a user-authored custom stdio server whose args literally contain "mcp-remote" can reach it.

MCPOAuth.swift:404-406 - the sign-in callback listener sets only `requiredLocalEndpoint = .hostPort(host: "127.0.0.1", port: .any)` and, unlike MCPProxy (:97), does not set `requiredInterfaceType = .loopback`. R037 records the endpoint but not the missing interface restriction, which is the kind of detail a port's socket-binding code has to decide.
thin_reports: R037 - not thin overall (MCPHub, MCPProbe, MCPProviderConfig and MCPBridgeSource are dense and mostly correct), but its MCPOAuth.swift entry is thin for a 929-line file: it paraphrases the verbatim callback-page SVG instead of capturing it, omits the base+detail error-message composition rule, omits `scopes_supported`, omits that `expires_at` is optional and that a session without it never refreshes, and omits that the callback listener does not restrict its interface type. That one file deserves a re-read.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD — R031 must re-read Hydra.swift for the prompt corpus verbatim and R014 must re-classify HydraRunMetricsView; R005 has one inverted tie-break rule and several undescribed behaviors in AppModel+Hydra.swift.
contradictions: R031 (Hydra.swift, state_owned) says "HydraPrompts.verificationMarkers (28 markers)" while its own feature_notes says "verificationMarkers (34 exact substrings...)" and lists 34. The source has exactly 34 entries (DroppyCode/Core/Models/Hydra.swift:1128-1137). The state_owned count is wrong.

R005 (AppModel+Hydra.swift, feature_notes) says "The head cap is [pair?.maxHeads, settings.hydraMaxHeads].compactMap{$0}.min(); with neither, heads run uncapped." R031 (Hydra.swift) says the opposite for the runtime effect: HydraLaunch.hasRoom uses `maxHeads ?? uncappedConcurrency` with uncappedConcurrency = 8 (Hydra.swift:168-173). A port following R005 alone would let unbounded heads run, which the source comment explicitly guards against (21 simultaneous heads forcing a force quit).

R005 (HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift) says model(named:) ties are "broken by the later position in registry.models(for:)". The source breaks ties toward the EARLIER position: `matches.max { ... return options.firstIndex(lhs)! > options.firstIndex(rhs)! }` makes the higher-index element compare as smaller, so max() returns the lowest-index option (DroppyCode/App/HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift:52-61). R052's unresolved "LinkTextVeil has no call site within the assigned four files" is answered by R051's bundle: LinkTextView owns `let streamVeil = LinkTextVeil()` and LinkParagraphView calls `streamVeil.update(view, active: markdownVeiled)` after every render and `streamVeil.detach(view)` in dismantleNSView. Symmetrically, R051's unresolved "who calls HydraHeadHoverPopover.show()/hide()" is answered by R052's bundle: MarkdownView's InlineText and ProseRunView, both on `.onContinuousHover`.

Because markdownProseRuns is always true, ProseRunView's rendering is what a reader sees for every finished reply: ballot-box task markers (U+2611 / U+2610), bullet U+2022 at depth 0 and U+25E6 deeper, no quote capsule rule, plain label colours. MarkdownBlockView's accent-coloured circles, capsule quote rule and SF-Symbol task markers appear only while a reply streams. R052 flagged the visual difference as possibly unintentional; for the port both renderings must exist and must switch on isStreaming.

Popover dismissal is implemented the same way five times and must be ported as one mechanism: an NSPopover with `behavior = .applicationDefined`, content pre-measured through a throwaway NSHostingView (fittingSize or intrinsicContentSize) and frozen with `setFixedContent(_:size:)`, plus NSEvent local monitors for keyCode 53 (Escape) and [.leftMouseDown, .rightMouseDown]. Sites: ChatBadge.BadgePopoverCoordinator, PromptEditor.PromptEditorPopover, LinkPopover (this one uses `.transient` and only an Escape monitor), HydraHeadHoverPopover (250 ms hover debounce, 300pt fixed width, 78pt height fallback), ComposerController's suggestions popover (NSSize(width: 340, height: min(340, 44 + max(itemCount,1) * 26))).

macOS primitives with no Windows equivalent, appearing across the family and needing one substitution strategy each: NSCursor push/pop stacks (TimelineMinimap, ProseRunView, MarkdownView.InlineText, FollowUpQueueTab), CADisplayLink at CAFrameRateRange(24,60,preferred 30) (StreamVeil, two clocks), CAReplicatorLayer dot fields (ComposerWorkingDots, also used by ChatBadge's attention overlay and HydraDelegationBlock's sweep), CASpringAnimation with mass 1 / stiffness 170 / damping 26 (AttachmentFlight), NSHapticFeedbackManager .alignment and .levelChange (EffortSlider drag stops, FollowUpQueueTab reorder and bundle), TextKit 1 vs TextKit 2 duality (ComposerTextView measures via textLayoutManager with a layoutManager fallback because its draw override forces TextKit 1; LinkTextView is TextKit 1 throughout).

Three separate caches key on whole message text and must be sized together in the port: MarkdownView.blockCache RecentCache limit 800, RichLink.prettyCache limit 1200, TableBlock.cellCache limit 1200, plus the fixed rings MarkdownView.streamingParses 48 slots and RichLink.streamingPretty 4 slots, TimelineBlockCache 24 threads LRU, TimelineMinimap.entryCache 400, DiffDetailCache 60, HydraDelegationBlock.readingCache 200, FileIndex.built RecentCache limit 2 with 60s freshness, FaviconCache.memory flushed wholesale at 300, LinkTitles titles flushed wholesale at 400 (with its `claimed` set never cleared, so post-flush ids can never be re-fetched).

Every editable surface keeps its edit state on ThreadRuntime rather than in the view, so the port must persist it the same way or editors will close on scroll: `runtime.messageEdit` (UserMessageRow / MessageEditor), `runtime.followUpEdit` (FollowUpQueueTab / FollowUpEditor), `runtime.followUpsCollapsed` (queue fold). All three survive the row being recycled by the lazy stack and the thread being left and re-entered.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD - the reports are broadly accurate and unusually detailed, but R024 states a clamp backwards, R025 gets the RowDrag API and the placement fingerprint wrong and misses a glyph difference, and R048's Chrome.swift entry omits token values the whole family depends on.
contradictions: R048 documents RowDrag.settle as `settle(order:heights:fallbackHeight:pastCentre:move:) -> Bool` whose `move` closure returns Bool and gates the crossing loop (E:/Droppy/reference/droppy-code/DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/RowDrag.swift:29-35, 45, 52). R025 records the same API as `settle(order:heights:fallbackHeight:swap:)` - wrong argument label, no `pastCentre`, and no mention that the closure's Bool return stops the walk. At the sidebar call site (DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:783-793) the trailing closure's value is `withAnimation(Self.slide) { model.moveThread(...) }`, and AppModel.swift:338 / :358 declare `moveThread(_:to:placeAfter:) -> Bool` and `moveInActivity(_:to:placeAfter:among:) -> Bool`. A port that makes the move closure return Void reorders forever past a refused move.

R024 says the FloatingSidebarPanel resize is clamped 'with the minimum size as the lower bound'. FloatingSidebarPanel.swift:75-76 applies `min(max(minSize, next), area - origin - margin)`: the outer `min` runs last, so in a chat area narrower than minSize + 2*margin the written size is BELOW minSize (240x320) and is persisted to settings.sidebarPanelSize on that same drag tick (line 77). This contradicts R024's own, correct description of the read-side clamp at lines 29-32, which does use `max(minSize, ...)` on both arms.

R049 names the preferences store for "sidebarWidth"/"sidebarStartsOpen" as `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`; R053 names the store for "wallpaperSoftness"/"wallpaperFile" as `WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard`. Neither says they are the same store: DroppyCode/App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift:28 is `nonisolated static var defaults: UserDefaults? { CaptureRun.defaults }`. Read together the two reports imply two separate suites.

R050 describes the running breath ring as what a Hydra head at work wears (HydraGlyph.swift:21-24, `isRunning`). R025 describes the sidebar helper row as showing 'its HydraGlyph at 14 pt before the title' with no qualification. SidebarView.swift:1358 constructs `HydraGlyph(persona:size:status:)` with no `isRunning`, while SidebarView.swift:1478 in HeadCardsRow passes `isRunning: info.status == .running`. The same running head therefore breathes on its card and does not breathe on its helper row; no report records the difference.

R053's purpose line calls AppTheme a '25-case theme enum' while its own key_symbols list and AppTheme.swift:15-40 both hold 26 cases (system through matrix). The palette table in the same report also lists 26 rows.
gaps: FloatingSidebarPanel.swift:75-77 - the resize path can write and persist a `sidebarPanelSize` smaller than `minSize` (240x320) when `area.width - origin.x - 12 < 240`; no report describes that escape, and R024 asserts the opposite. Also unstated: the resize clamp is anchored on `origin` (the live `dragOrigin ?? rest`), so resizing while the panel is mid-drag clamps against the dragged origin, not the resting one.
SidebarView.swift:1358 - SidebarHelperRow's head glyph omits `isRunning`, so a running Hydra head shows no breath ring in the helper row. Unrecorded by R025 and R050.

SidebarView.swift:1872 - every thread row carries `.accessibilityValue(Text(isSettled ? "Settled" : ""))`. R025 enumerates the accessibility labels/values for SettledHeader, ActivityViewToggle, SettleCheck, the fold button and the helper stub, but not this one.

SidebarView.swift:2484-2520 - R025 calls the PlacementCache fingerprint an '18-field Fingerprint'. It has 17 fields (id, projectID, parentThreadID, isArchived, isInPanel, isSettled, settledAt, isPinned, sortOrder, activityOrder, activityOrderDay, createdAt, updatedAt, foldsHelpers, isHydraHead, hydraIndex, hasUnread), identical to ThreadPlacement's. A port sizing the invalidation key off the report gets it wrong.

Chrome.swift:178,180 - the exact glass tint on every capsule and circle in the app, `.regular.tint(Chrome.glassTint.opacity(0.3))`, is absent from R048; the report records only '.glassEffect(.regular.tint(...).interactive(), in:)'. The 0.3 is the one number that decides how much theme colour every chrome control carries.

Chrome.swift:618-646 - R048 lists `SidebarSymbol` and `SidebarIconBadge` in key_symbols but records no metrics for either, though every sidebar row, project row, badge and bottom row draws through them: SidebarSymbol is `.resizable().interpolation(.high).aspectRatio(contentMode: .fit).frame(width: Chrome.symbolSize * scale, height: ...).symbolRenderingMode(.monochrome)` with symbolSize 14; SidebarIconBadge is `.foregroundStyle(Chrome.primaryText.opacity(0.85)).frame(width: 20, height: 20)`. The 0.85 is why sidebar glyphs sit below title contrast.

Chrome.swift:1061-1069 - WindowDragView overrides `acceptsFirstMouse(for:) -> true` and swallows mouse-up with an empty `mouseUp` override. R048's side_effects mention only `performDrag(with:)`. The empty mouseUp is what stops a drag-release from reaching SwiftUI behind the sidebar.

Chrome.swift:10 sets `sheetInset = 0`, which makes every branch of RootView.swift:40-42 evaluate to zero padding: `.padding(.leading, sidebar.isVisible && !onlyFloats ? 0 : Chrome.sheetInset)`, `.padding(.trailing, 0)`, `.padding(.vertical, 0)`. R020 describes this conditional as live layout behavior without classifying it as currently inert; a port would faithfully implement a branch that does nothing today.

R049 leaves `titlebarHeight`, `collapsedTrafficLightTop` and `trafficLightsFitWidth` symbolic because Chrome is in another bundle, and R048 leaves the trafficLight* tokens as 'consumed elsewhere'. Nobody in the family closes the loop, yet these are the exact numbers a Windows custom caption bar needs: titlebarHeight = 0 + 12 + 32 = 44, collapsedTrafficLightTop = 0 + 12 + (32-14)/2 = 21, trafficLightsFitWidth = 18 + 60 + 10 = 88, trafficLightPitch = 23.

DroppyCode/Core/Support/CaptureRun.swift:10-40 - R049 and R053 both leave the defaults suite unresolved. `CaptureRun.defaults` is nil on a normal launch (everything lands in UserDefaults.standard) and only becomes `UserDefaults(suiteName: "iordv.droppycode.website-captures")` when the process is launched with the exact flags `--website-captures <folder>` or `--tour-captures <folder>`. Exact command-line flags were in scope for this read and no report in the family captured them, nor the fact that a capture run also redirects storage to `<folder>/storage` and never touches the Keychain.

settings.settledCollapsed has an undocumented default and an undocumented key. AppSettings.swift:712 reads `defaults.object(forKey: Key.settledCollapsed) as? Bool ?? true` and AppSettings.swift:133 defines that key as the string "settledSectionCollapsed", not "settledCollapsed". R025 lists the property and says it 'survives relaunch' but gives neither. The default decides that on a fresh install the whole settled list is never built (SidebarView.swift:531 `if collapsed { break }`).

settings.sidebarPanelOrigin / sidebarPanelSize persist as `[Double]` arrays, not as points/sizes: AppSettings.swift:652-672 writes `[origin.x, origin.y]` and `[size.width, size.height]` and calls `removeObject` on nil; AppSettings.swift:764-772 reads them back element-wise. R024 records only 'CGPoint?/CGSize?, nil default', so the on-disk shape and what happens to a malformed or short array are unstated.

AppModel.swift:377-379 - `settledFirst` is `(lhs.settledAt ?? lhs.updatedAt) > (rhs.settledAt ?? rhs.updatedAt)`. R025 leaves it as 'latest settled first' in unresolved_questions and never records the updatedAt fallback, which is exactly the migration behaviour for threads settled before settledAt was persisted.

R019 leaves three answerable questions open that decide user-visible strings: ShortcutStore.label(for:) is optional (RootView.swift:466 uses `if let chord = ShortcutStore.label(for: .newThread)`), and AppModel.swift:846-854 gives the palette's finish row its literal title and symbol - "Reopen thread" with "arrow.uturn.backward" when the finish action is .settle and the selected thread is settled, otherwise "<Settle|Archive> thread" with "checkmark.circle" or "archivebox". Left open, the command palette's finish row has no specified label.

KeyChord.allowedModifiers is left unresolved by both R025 and R029, yet it gates two shipped key paths: the archive popover's local monitor (SidebarView.swift:950) and ThreadWindow's Cmd-digit monitor (ThreadWindow.swift:13) and Escape close (ThreadWindow.swift:50). DroppyCode/Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:6 defines it as `[.control, .option, .shift, .command]` - i.e. Fn, CapsLock and the numeric-pad flag are deliberately ignored.

AppTheme.swift:221-226 - `ThemeManager.current`'s didSet rebuilds spec and posts `ThemeManager.didChange` unconditionally, including when the same theme value is reassigned. R053 says it posts 'on every assignment' but does not flag that a no-op write re-tints every layer-backed spinner cell (WorkingIndicators.swift) and every HydraButton observer.

Popovers.swift:110 - `PopoverMenu` applies `.presentedChrome()` itself, so every ellipsis menu, chrome menu and picker popover carries capsule button shape and the theme tint. R048 documents presentedChrome() as a standalone modifier and as applied by setFixedContent, but not that PopoverMenu carries it.

Popovers.swift:262-273 vs :369-375 - the same RowAction runs with different timing in its two presentations. PopoverItem closes the popover first and defers `action()` into a following `Task { @MainActor in ... }` (so a sheet-presenting action survives), while RowActionMenuButtons calls `item.action()` synchronously inside the menu callback. Neither R048 nor R025 records the asymmetry, although the sidebar depends on it: the context-menu Settle posts `model.finishRequest` (SidebarView.swift:2288) while the popover Settle calls the row's own `settle()` (SidebarView.swift:2225).

SidebarView.swift:1462 and :846-849 - HeadCardsRow computes `cardRows = rows.count + (capped ? 1 : 0)`, so a head card with more than 12 heads is one glyph row taller for the chevron. The drag slot fallback in slotHeights uses `headCardHeight(rows: (headCount + 5) / 6)` and never adds that chevron row, so before the card has reported a measured height the reorder slot under-measures a capped card. R025 records the 12 cap and the headCardHeight formula but not the extra row.

Four independent window-level overlays draw in the same named coordinate space "droppy-code-window", established once at RootView.swift:68: GenieLayer (archive flights and Hydra panel morphs), RowGlideLayer (settle/reopen ghosts), CommandPalette and FloatingSidebarPanel. Reduce Motion is a global kill switch across this family, not a per-animation nicety: Chrome.panelSlide and Chrome.settleFlight swap to easeOut 0.18 / 0.20 (Chrome.swift:97-112), SidebarLayout.slideRun drops 420ms -> 220ms (WindowChrome.swift:270), traffic-light placement drops 0.32 -> 0.18 (WindowChrome.swift:221), RowGlideAnimator.launch refuses to fly at all (RowGlide.swift:76), GenieAnimator.launch and morph return false so the caller shows the real thing (Genie.swift:62, 81), HydraBreathRing installs no animation, the spinners freeze at their per-cell phase, and SettleGlideModifier fades in place. On Windows this is SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION, and it must be read in all nine places or the port's motion is inconsistent.

Two animations depend on rasterizing a live SwiftUI tree to a bitmap: RowGlideAnimator.render (RowGlide.swift:131-137) and GenieAnimator.launch (Genie.swift:84-87), both via ImageRenderer at `NSScreen.main?.backingScaleFactor ?? 2`. The ghost faces are re-rendered from ThreadRowFace with a deliberately different trailingClearance from the live row (SidebarView.swift:1944-1946), and MiniSpinner ships a separate `isStill: true` shapes-only variant (WorkingIndicators.swift:84-88) purely because ImageRenderer cannot capture AppKit views. Any port needs a view-to-bitmap capture with the same two-face + still-spinner discipline, or the settle/reopen/archive animations cannot be reproduced.

DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow and DCNotificationGuard are pure macOS 26/27 AppKit exception nets (private `_postWindowNeeds*` overrides; NSNotificationCenter post swizzling) with no Windows analogue. They are load-bearing on macOS but must not be re-implemented; the port should record that every NSWindow subclass in the app derives from the guarded base only for that reason, and that ThreadWindow/SecondaryWindow behaviour is the part worth porting.

No theme in AppTheme defines a text colour. Chrome.primaryText and Chrome.secondaryText are the dynamic system colours `NSColor.labelColor` / `.secondaryLabelColor` (Chrome.swift:76-77), and Chrome.overlay(_:) is primaryText at an opacity - so every row fill, card fill, divider and panel scrim in the family is derived from the system label colour, not from the theme. The .system theme's surface is itself a dynamic NSColor resolving sRGB 1E1E20 in dark and FFFFFF in light (AppTheme.swift:180-187). A Windows port must choose its own primaryText/secondaryText equivalents before any of the 26 palettes mean anything.

Sidebar launch state and session state are deliberately separate: `sidebarStartsOpen` ("sidebarStartsOpen", default false) is the only thing read at launch and is written only from the Settings toggle, while `toggle()` and `endDrag()` persist `sidebarWidth` (default 268, clamped 210...440) from restingWidth and never touch startsOpen (WindowChrome.swift:286-370). The sidebar therefore always starts collapsed on a fresh install regardless of how the last session ended.

verdict: COHERENT - every claim I re-checked against the source held up (literals, strings, control flow, SF Symbol names, state machines), so no file needs a re-read; what is missing is a set of specific deferred constants, three unguarded destructive/re-entrant paths, and two capture-mode / cross-file call sites that the family never resolved.
cross_cutting_findings: Escape is detected by the raw macOS keyCode 53 in FIVE separate places in this family, each with a different swallow policy, and no report compares them: DiffInspector.swift:663-667 (DiffPopoverCoordinator.handleKeyDown closes and returns nil), TerminalPanel.swift:335-341 (TerminalHost closes the drawer and returns nil, but only when foregroundJobIsTheShell and no KeyChord.allowedModifiers are held and the terminal view is firstResponder), MCPKeyPanel.swift:65-71 and MCPSetupPanel.swift:86-92 (both close the panel and return nil while visible), ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:601-604 (cancels the recording, and its monitor swallows EVERY keyDown/keyUp/flagsChanged while recording). All five are NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents, which has no Windows equivalent; the port needs five separate decisions, not one.

DiffPopoverCoordinator's mouse monitor is the one place that deliberately does NOT swallow: DiffInspector.swift:657-660 closes the popover on a left/right mouseDown outside the popover's content window but still returns the event, so the same click also activates its target (another turn's Review button opens that diff in one tap). A port that consumes the dismiss click breaks that flow. R018 states it; nobody else in the family generalizes it.

Four distinct AppKit top-level surfaces here, all borderless/chromeless with the same recipe: TourWindowController HostWindow (styleMask [.borderless,.fullSizeContentView], canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain overridden true, isOpaque false, backgroundColor .clear, hasShadow true, level .floating, collectionBehavior [.managed,.participatesInCycle,.fullScreenAuxiliary], isMovableByWindowBackground true, isReleasedWhenClosed false), MCPKeyPanel and MCPSetupPanel NSPanels (styleMask [.nonactivatingPanel,.fullSizeContentView,.titled,.closable], titleVisibility .hidden, titlebarAppearsTransparent, level .floating, hidesOnDeactivate false, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces,.fullScreenAuxiliary], all three standardWindowButtons hidden), and the NSPopover in DiffPopoverCoordinator (behavior .semitransient, animates true, fixed 640x540). All rely on AppKit shaping the shadow to the window's alpha so it follows the rounded card.

Pre-measuring SwiftUI content with a throwaway NSHostingView before the window appears is used three times and is load-bearing each time: TourWindowController.maxBottomPanelHeight (layoutSubtreeIfNeeded + fittingSize.height, max across pages, so the tour card never resizes between pages), MCPKeyPanel.present (fittingSize.height.rounded(.up), floor 100, width 380), MCPSetupPanel.present (same, width 400). MCPSetupPanel additionally re-fits at runtime through onGeometryChange -> fit(height:), which moves origin.y by (oldHeight - wanted) so the TOP edge stays fixed.

Chrome.* design tokens are deferred as "defined elsewhere" by R018, R021, R022, R023 and R026, but they are plain literals in DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift and should be captured once for the whole port: windowCornerRadius 26, sheetInset 0 (so the Settings detail pane has ZERO inset), sheetCornerRadius 16, trafficLightDiameter 14, trafficLightSpacing 9, trafficLightLeading 18, trafficLightTop 16, trafficLightClearance 10, chromeHorizontalPadding 14, chromeTopPadding 12, capsuleContentHeight 28, capsuleVerticalPadding 2, capsuleHorizontalPadding 12, capsuleHeight = 28 + 2*2 = 32 (computed, Chrome.swift:38), symbolSize 14, listInset 10, sectionSpacing 20, sectionHeaderSpacing 10, contentHorizontalPadding 16, rowControlTrailingPadding 10, rowButtonLabelHeight 16.

NSHapticFeedbackManager is used in three of this family's files and the shared `enum Haptics` is DEFINED in ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:482-486, not in a utilities file: ShortcutsSettingsPage (.alignment on a modifier added, .generic on a rejected chord and on Clear / Reset to default, .levelChange on an accepted chord), AboutUpdateViews (.alignment and .levelChange in startCelebrationSweep), ModelsSettingsPage (NSHapticFeedbackManager .alignment on every landed drag-reorder swap). The Terminal subsystem's hardest macOS dependency is not SwiftTerm but TerminalStore.swift:69-77: `foregroundJobIsTheShell(_:)` reads kinfo_proc via sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, shell) and returns `info.kp_eproc.e_tpgid == info.kp_eproc.e_pgid`, because the pty master answers no tcgetpgrp for a process it is not the controlling terminal of. This single predicate gates whether Escape closes the drawer or reaches vim/claude/less. On Windows (ConPTY) there is no process-group concept at all, so the Escape-at-prompt rule needs a different mechanism, not a translation.

The login-shell launch contract is exact and must be ported literally or replaced consciously (TerminalStore.swift:28-40): executable = LoginEnvironment.userShell(), execName = "-" + shell.lastPathComponent, currentDirectory = the project directory, environment = LoginEnvironment.current overridden with TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, TERM_PROGRAM=Droppy Code, DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT=<directory>, flattened to "KEY=VALUE" strings; args are [] with no command, and exactly ["-l", "-i", "-c", "<command>; exec <shell> -l"] for a script tab.

Persisted state this family writes is all AppSettings/UserDefaults with literal key names, plus two non-UserDefaults stores: MCP secrets in the Keychain (locked variables, via model.mcp.saveCustomValues) and non-secret custom-server variable values in mcp.json (the lock toggle's own help string says so: "Stored in mcp.json; click to keep it in the Keychain instead"). gaps: DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:626-632 - R018 states the order of show() backwards. The source is `guard let runtime, let target = resolvedAnchor() else { return }` THEN `session += 1` THEN `guard !popover.isShown else { return }`. R018's feature_notes say "show() guards on a resolved anchor and on the popover not already being shown, bumps session". The order matters: every show() call while the popover is already shown still increments `session` without touching `pendingSession`, so the stale-close guard in popoverDidClose (session == pendingSession) fails and that close will NOT clear shownRuntime.isDiffVisible and will NOT set popover.contentViewController = nil. setAnchor(_:) and setFallbackAnchor(_:) both call show() unconditionally when desiredVisible, so this is reachable in normal use.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD - R036 is dense and mostly accurate on the small files, but Git.swift carries two outright wrong claims (an `add -A` timeout, and an unreachable error string presented as shipped UI text), omits the exact argument vectors of six shipped commands, and leaves the checkpoint commit's parentless shape, its two `phase` literals and the git/forge-CLI identity split undocumented.
contradictions: TIMEOUT, report vs source. R036 (Git.swift feature_notes) states 'default timeout 120 s, 300 s for push, fetch, pull, worktree add, the forge CLIs, `add -A` and diff.' Git.swift:164 `commitAll(message:)` runs `["add", "-A"]` with NO timeout argument, i.e. the 120 s default. Only the scratch/throwaway-index adds take 300 (lines 253, 448, 459, 484, 707). A port copying the report would give the user-facing commit path a 300 s budget it does not have.

UNREACHABLE STRING, report vs source. R036 ui_elements for Git.swift lists 'Error text surfaced to the user: "The request could not be merged."'. In Git.swift:212-226 `lastFailure` is initialised to that literal but overwritten with `result.failureMessage` on every failed attempt, and the loop `for attempt in 0..<6` always executes at least once; Shell.swift:15-19 guarantees `failureMessage` is never empty (it falls back to "The command failed with exit code \(status)."). The literal is dead code, not user-visible text. R036 did not classify it.

SCRATCH-INDEX FALLBACK, report vs source. R036 says currentTree's capture closure, 'when scratch is nil or the incremental add fails it deletes the scratch, re-seeds by copying the real index (or read-tree HEAD) and runs `add -A -- .`'. Git.swift:434-438: when `scratch` is nil the closure returns `try await captureTree()`, which builds a *fresh* `droppy-code-index-<UUID>` under temporaryDirectory and removes it in a defer (lines 471-487); it never touches the shared scratch. The delete-and-reseed path is only inside `captureTree(scratch:paths:)` (Git.swift:452-461), where `scratch` is non-optional.
cross_cutting_findings: Two git identities, never distinguished by R036. `Git.commitWork(_:parent:message:)` (Git.swift:268-272) runs `commit-tree <tree> -p <parent> -F -` with the message on stdin and WITHOUT `Self.identity`, so a head's branch commit carries the user's own git config identity. `commitTree(_:message:)` (Git.swift:668-673) and `captureCheckpoint` (Git.swift:423) both pass `environment: Self.identity`, forcing GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="Droppy Code" and GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="droppy-code@localhost". R036 lists commitWork only as a key_symbol and never states its flags or that it is the one commit path left in the user's name.

Checkpoint commits are PARENTLESS. Git.swift:423 is `run(["commit-tree", tree, "-m", "Droppy Code checkpoint"], environment: Self.identity)` with no `-p`. Contrast Git.swift:669-670 (`commitTree`) which appends `["-p", "HEAD"]` when `hasCommits()`. R036 describes commitTree's parent rule but says only that captureCheckpoint 'runs commit-tree with the message'. For the port this matters: checkpoints are root commits reachable solely through `refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/...`, so ref deletion (Git.swift:651-658) makes them immediately gc-able.

Forge CLIs run in a different environment from git. `Shell.run(tool:)` calls in Git.swift:181, 186, 191 and 215-217 pass no `environment:`, so Shell.swift:49 substitutes `LoginEnvironment.current` WITHOUT the GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 / GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 that `Git.run` (Git.swift:37-38) always sets. glab/gh/tea can therefore prompt on a terminal where git never would. R036 listed this as unresolved rather than reading Shell.swift.

Missing forge CLI throws an exact string R036 left unresolved: Shell.swift:129-131, `guard let executable = LoginEnvironment.which(name) else { throw ShellError("\(name) was not found on your PATH.") }`. That is the message a user without gh/glab/tea sees from createPullRequest and mergePullRequest.

macOS-only git resolution nobody flagged concretely. `LoginEnvironment.git` (Shell.swift:394-409) is `resolvedGit` else `which("git")` else `/usr/bin/git`; `developerGit` runs `/usr/bin/xcode-select -p` with an 8 s timeout and prefers `<developer>/usr/bin/git` over the `/usr/bin/git` shim (the comment cites 11.5 ms vs 4.5 ms per call). `which` splits PATH on ":" (Shell.swift:417). Every one of these is a Windows port decision and R036's platform_assumptions only says 'git is invoked as an executable URL from LoginEnvironment.git'.

`Git.run` never passes `outputLimit`, so every git invocation buffers stdout/stderr unbounded (Shell.swift:36-44, `outputLimit: Int? = nil`). R036's only size note is the 40,000-character truncation inside `workingChanges()`, which is a caller-side trim, not a capture bound. A binary `diff --binary` over a large tree (Git.swift:544-570) is read whole into memory.
gaps: Git.swift:409 `checkpointRef(thread:turn:phase:)` - R036 documents the ref template but never names the only two `phase` values shipped: "start" (ThreadRuntime.swift:1226) and "end" (ThreadRuntime.swift:2281). Nor does it name the persisted fields that hold the resulting ref strings, `Turn.baseCheckpoint` (set ThreadRuntime.swift:1250, read ThreadRuntime.swift:1773) and `Turn.endCheckpoint` (ThreadRuntime.swift:2282, read :1775). Migration behaviour of those two persisted strings across a rename of the ref namespace is stated nowhere.

Exact argument vectors missing for six shipped commands that R036 only lists as symbols: Git.swift:290 `fetch()` = `["fetch", "--quiet", "origin"]` (timeout 300); Git.swift:300 `changedPaths(from:to:)` = `["diff", "--name-only", "-z", from, to]`; Git.swift:260 `treeHash(of:)` = `["rev-parse", "<ref>^{tree}"]`; Git.swift:264 `commitHash(of:)` = `["rev-parse", "--verify", ref]` with an undocumented default parameter `ref: String = "HEAD"`; Git.swift:269 `commitWork` = `["commit-tree", tree, "-p", parent, "-F", "-"]`; Git.swift:294 `isAncestor` = `["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, other]`. The bundle's own rule is that exact flags are the specification.

Git.swift:544-570 `diff(from:to:binary:paths:)` boundary unstated. R036 says it 'chunks pathspecs at diffPathChunk = 400 per invocation'; the guard is `paths.count > Self.diffPathChunk`, so exactly 400 paths is a single call. More importantly `paths: []` (non-nil, empty) still prepends `--literal-pathspecs` and appends a bare `--`, producing a full-tree diff, with no early return of the kind `resetIndex` (Git.swift:392), `checkoutPaths` (:398), `removePaths` (:403), `restore` (:602) and `previewRestore` (:577) all have. Shipped callers guard (AppModel+Hydra.swift:726, ThreadRuntime.swift:3289), so this is unreachable today, but the port needs the rule written down.

R036's unresolved_question 'isBuildOutput has no call site inside this bundle' is answerable: seven shipped call sites, all silent filters that drop the path with no user-visible report.
